# Model-server extract for the paper (auto-generated by `exp03/paper_extract.py`)

Conventions used everywhere below: **mIoU and Dice are the means over all 4 classes including background** (the trainer's Evaluator; background IoU is about 0.999, which lifts both). Checkpoint rule: **best-validation-mIoU epoch; the test split is evaluated once, at that epoch** (never the final epoch, never the best-test checkpoint). Final statistics: seeds 43/44/45, **sample std (ddof=1)**; exp03_summary.md reports the population std (ddof=0), which is smaller by a factor 0.816. Seed 42 is the tuning seed and is excluded. All results are on the **block-max-pooled emulation** of the small RD map (see section 4), not on SoC-FFT data. The paper skeleton `radar_paper_skeleton_v5_fpga_results.tex` is not on this server, so values are keyed by the field names in the instruction file.

## 2. Final proposed-model headline values

**MAC check (instruction asks to verify 4.95 M).** The 23-layer topology matches the paper (20 layers map directly, 3 are channel-padded to Ti=To=8: `stem.dw`, `stem.pw`, `head_out`; same for both widths). But the 4.95 M MACs belong to the **1.0x-width** network (4,952,576 MACs, 31,139 params). The model Exp03 selected at R64-D8 under the pre-set rule is the **0.5x-width** network (1,569,280 MACs, 9,587 params). They are **not the same export**, so 4.95 M must not be reused for the Exp03 headline. The 1.0x network lost the tie-break only on cost: on the tuning seed its validation mIoU was 0.5729 vs 0.5772 for 0.5x (inside the 0.01 tie band), so the rule picked the cheaper 0.5x. The 1.0x network was therefore trained afterwards with final seeds 43/44/45 (`exp03/run_w10_finals.py`; FP32 LR 1e-3, QAT LR 1e-5 chosen on seed-42 validation mIoU from {1e-4, 3e-5, 1e-5}), so the hardware-side 4.95 M model has its own accuracy rows (Sec. 7 and 8c). The older NPU-server checkpoint `checkpoints/8x64_maxpool_0.6122_bc64` has the 1.0x architecture (default width, stem_stride 1) but a different training (tvt normalization).

- `FINAL_MODEL_NAME` = KuRALSNetNPUSeg 0.5x (stem_stride 1, encoder_depth 1, bottleneck k=3, eltwise add linear)
- `FINAL_RD_RESOLUTION` = R64-D8
- `FINAL_PARAMETER_COUNT` = 9,587 (torch learnable = conv weights + BN gamma/beta; equals int8 weights + int16 scale + int16 bias entries)
- `FINAL_MAC_COUNT` = 1,569,280

Semantic metric recommendation: **mIoU (4-class mean incl. background)** with Dice and UAV-IoU alongside, because mIoU is the selection metric of every Exp03 run (`select_metric: miou`), the metric of Tables A/B/C and of the QAT study. UAV IoU is the most operationally meaningful single number but has the highest variance; quote it as a secondary column.

## 4. Training / evaluation methodology

- **dataset**: KuRALS-CW only (continuous-wave radar). KuRALS-PD is not used by Exp03.
- **classes / IDs**: 4 channels: 0 background, 1 UAV, 2 and 3 non-UAV (pedestrian / vehicle of the single airport sequence). Class 3 has about 0.04 labelled cells per frame (D8), so its IoU is very noisy.
- **splits**: Per-recording **chronological** split 80/10/10 (first 80 % of each of the 9 recordings = train, next 10 % = validation, last 10 % = test; the airport recording is split in two blocks, frames 0-199 and 200+). Not random, not by recording. Samples (1 frame each, n_frames=1): {'Train': (2064, 9), 'Validation': (258, 9), 'Test': (264, 9)}. Identical frame lists at D8/D16/D32.
- **input**: One RD frame, shape 1 x Doppler x 64 range. Native map 124 Doppler x 2048 range (Doppler raw bins [2:126] of 128).
- **RD resolution conversion**: Block max-pooling of the linear-magnitude map over contiguous near-equal bin groups (`np.array_split`, `kurals/dataset_process/resize_extracted_dataset.py`, same code for all three). Range 2048 -> 64: exactly 32 bins per cell. **Doppler 124 -> 8 / 16 / 32: groups of 15-16 / 7-8 / 3-4 bins** (not an integer ratio, so group sizes differ by one). The result is an emulation of the SoC grid (which uses its own small FFT from raw samples; no raw IQ here).
- **label conversion**: Dense masks are not resampled as images: every foreground cell of the native one-hot mask is remapped through the same bin lookup; background = complement; dilate_radius = 0 (no label dilation at any resolution).
- **normalisation**: norm_type `dsp_log`: DSP 5.3-bit log2 code q = clamp(log8(uint32(floor(P)) >> 16) - 0, 0, 127), fed with input_scale 1.0; Doppler axis ifftshifted to natural FFT order for input and labels. Same for all models, resolutions and stages.
- **augmentation**: `hflip,vflip` on the training split only (random horizontal and vertical flips, applied to the stored layout before the DSP code and ifftshift). No gain/noise jitter.
- **loss**: `nbs1`: NBS1-recalibrated per-pixel cross-entropy (threshold 0.05, degree 1), unweighted; no Dice term.
- **optimizer**: AdamW, weight_decay = 0 (config default; no weight decay was set in any Exp03 run).
- **base learning rate**: FP32: Exp A one common LR chosen on seed 42 from {3e-3, 2e-3, 1e-3, 3e-4} = 0.001; Exp B per-resolution LR from {1e-3, 3.33e-4} (see section 6); KuRALS-Net 0.003; QAT D8: 0.0001, D16: 0.0001, D32: 0.0001 (grid {1e-4, 3e-5, 1e-5}, chosen on seed 42).
- **LR scheduler**: Cosine annealing (`CosineAnnealingLR`, T_max = epochs - 1, eta_min 1e-7), stepped per epoch; no warm-up.
- **maximum epochs**: FP32 200; QAT fine-tune 100 (from the best-val FP32 checkpoint).
- **early stopping**: None. All epochs run; the best-validation epoch is kept.
- **batch size**: physical 6, accumulation 1, effective 6 for every model and resolution.
- **seed policy**: Seed 42 = tuning seed (LR search, Exp B candidate choice, QAT LR choice). Seeds 43/44/45 = final seeds; torch and numpy seeds are set equal to the run seed. Mean/std over the three final seeds only.
- **validation frequency**: Every 600 iterations (about every 1.8 epochs at 338 iterations/epoch); test is computed at the same time but only read at the best-validation epoch.
- **checkpoint selection**: Highest validation mIoU (`select_metric: miou`); the trainer's best-test checkpoint exists but is never used.
- **test evaluation**: Test metrics at the best-validation epoch, reported once per seed; final-epoch numbers are never reported.

## 6. Experiment B: resolution-specific NPU-oriented winners

Rule (fixed before training): identical grid at every resolution (width {0.5, 1.0, 1.5} x stem_stride {1, 2} x LR {1e-3, 3.33e-4}); candidates whose peak NPU buffer exceeds 32,768 B are logged and not trained; winner = highest seed-42 validation mIoU, ties within 0.01 -> fewer MACs.

| resolution | width | stem stride | LR | val mIoU (seed 42) | test mIoU | test Dice | params | MACs | peak NPU buffer | <=32 KB |

| R64-D8 | 0.5 | 1 | 0.0003333 | 0.5772 | 0.5212 $\pm$ 0.0675 | 0.6119 $\pm$ 0.1008 | 9,587 | 1,569,280 | 16,384 | yes |
| R64-D16 | 0.5 | 1 | 0.001 | 0.5620 | 0.4646 $\pm$ 0.0676 | 0.5502 $\pm$ 0.0734 | 9,587 | 3,138,560 | 32,768 | yes |

```latex
R64-D8 & 0.5 & 1 & 0.00033 & 0.5212 $\pm$ 0.0675 & 0.6119 $\pm$ 0.1008 & 1.57 & 16 \\
R64-D16 & 0.5 & 1 & 0.001 & 0.4646 $\pm$ 0.0676 & 0.5502 $\pm$ 0.0734 & 3.14 & 32 \\
R64-D32 & 0.5 & 2 & 0.00033 & 0.2931 $\pm$ 0.0150 & 0.3273 $\pm$ 0.0250 & 1.57 & 16 \\
```

**Flags.** (1) The D32 winner uses stem_stride 2 (the 1.0x/1.5x stride-1 options exceed 32 KB), i.e. the output head runs at /2 and every 2x2 block is identical, which is why its mIoU is only about 0.29; this is a buffer-limit effect, not evidence about D32 information content. (2) The D16 winner sits **exactly at the 32,768 B limit** (no headroom). (3) "Feasible" means `gen_cfg.py` (NPU8, PF=8) allocated the network within 32 KB buffers; **none of the D16/D32 winners has been run on the NPU or the FPGA**, so execution on hardware is unverified. The D8 winner has the released int8 export and replay but also no board run in this repo.

## 8. FP32 vs QAT (paired per seed)

QAT start: the best-validation FP32 checkpoint of the same seed and design; 100 epochs (33,800 iterations) of fine-tuning at the LR chosen on seed 42 (1e-4 at every resolution), same cosine schedule shape, same batch and data. Quantization: int8 symmetric per-tensor activations with EMA observers, per-channel weights with hardware w_eff = 2w+1, int16 scale/bias, truncating shifts (bias_shift in [5,20], act_shift in [0,7]), stem input scale fixed to 1.0 (DSP code). **Observer-enable period: fake-quant and observers are active from iteration 0 (quant_warmup_iters = 0) until the freeze at iteration 24,000 (about epoch 71 of 100); BN-freeze: none (BN is folded from running statistics at every forward and is not frozen).** The previously collapsed QAT runs (fixed 15,000-iteration warm-up, 8x64-tuned schedule) are not used anywhere.

**Interpretation caveat.** QAT is 100 more epochs of fine-tuning from the FP32 checkpoint, so FP32 - QAT alone cannot be read as a quantization cost; the matched control in 8b separates the two effects.

### 8b. Matched FP32-continuation control

Same start checkpoint, LR, epochs, schedule, seeds and selection rule as the QAT stage, quantization never enabled (`exp03/run_fp32_control.py`, tags `F_...`). Quantization cost = FP32-continuation - QAT; training effect = FP32-continuation - FP32.

| res | FP32 | FP32-cont | QAT | cont - FP32 (training effect) | cont - QAT (quantization cost) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D8 | 0.5212 $\pm$ 0.0675 | 0.5176 $\pm$ 0.0693 | 0.5965 $\pm$ 0.0600 | -0.0036 $\pm$ 0.0058 | -0.0789 $\pm$ 0.0322 |
| D16 | 0.4646 $\pm$ 0.0676 | 0.4659 $\pm$ 0.0637 | 0.5076 $\pm$ 0.0925 | +0.0014 $\pm$ 0.0205 | -0.0417 $\pm$ 0.0533 |
| D32 | 0.2931 $\pm$ 0.0150 | 0.2748 $\pm$ 0.0163 | 0.3213 $\pm$ 0.0307 | -0.0184 $\pm$ 0.0184 | -0.0465 $\pm$ 0.0443 |
**Result.** Continuing FP32 training for the same 100 epochs changes test mIoU by less than 0.02 at every resolution (mean change -0.004, +0.001, -0.018), so the extra training is **not** what lifts the QAT models; the int8 QAT models still score higher than the matched FP32 continuation (mean +0.079, +0.042, +0.046 for D8/D16/D32), with a spread (per-resolution std 0.03-0.05) comparable to the gap at D16/D32. This is not a measured quantization cost: the data show no accuracy loss from int8 QAT relative to FP32. A plausible but **untested** cause is that QAT folds BN from running statistics in every forward (matching evaluation), whereas FP32 training uses noisy batch-6 BN statistics and is evaluated with the running ones. Until that is tested, describe the FP32 rows as a reference that may under-represent the architecture.

*Peak activation* (padded in+out of the largest layer) of the proposed stride-1 network is **larger** than NPU-UNet 0.5x's because it runs stem..dec_a at full 8x64 resolution; the ratio is therefore below 1 for the small U-Net. The NPU allocator watermark (peak NPU buffer) is the hardware-relevant figure; compare it with the same caution.

Dominance check (a point dominates another only if it is no worse on both axes and strictly better on one; FP32 mIoU vs cost):

- vs MACs: points dominating the proposed model: none. Pareto-optimal on this axis pair among the measured points.
- vs peak activation: points dominating the proposed model: NPU-UNet 0.5x, NPU-UNet 1.0x. NOT Pareto-optimal on this axis pair.
- vs peak NPU buffer: points dominating the proposed model: NPU-UNet 0.5x, NPU-UNet 1.0x. NOT Pareto-optimal on this axis pair.

## 11. Flags for the paper author

- The FPGA/hardware numbers were measured on the 4.95 M-MAC (1.0x) network; the Exp03-selected model is the 1.57 M-MAC (0.5x) network. Both now have final-seed FP32 + QAT rows (Sec. 7, 8, 8c). The 1.0x QAT LR (1e-5) was chosen on seed-42 validation like the others; no FP32-continuation control was run for 1.0x, and no int8 release/replay package was built for it (only for 0.5x, `exp03/model_release_v01`). The paper must state which of the two models is the deployed one.
- Seed variance is large (seed 43 is a weak FP32 run at every resolution); most between-resolution and between-model gaps are within one standard deviation.
- Resolution results use pooled-native emulation, not the SoC small-FFT signal.
- Class 3 is nearly absent; per-class IoU for it is not reportable as a robust number.
- Latency: no NPU cycle/latency numbers exist on this server for any model.
